scope: Proposition F.4 (Sign transfer) of the manuscript “Uniform Cartier sections for Fano type contractions” (preprints/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 066 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d97ba60373419ba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 76. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose w is common h-lc and w(fj) = 0 for every j. Let g = U/hb, where 0 ̸= U ∈ OS,x, b ∈ N>0, and w(g) = 0. Let Q be the actual common slice and Q0 the common slice defined by h̄ and the ¯ fj on S0. Then q(g) ≤ 0 (q ∈ Q) ⇐⇒ q0 (ḡ) ≤ 0 (q0 ∈ Q0 ). (F.7) One may add any finite list of tests of value zero at w. There is no bound on the degree or the cost of g in this statement.
